role.instructions: The state is a user's request to a coding agent, split into numbered items. Classify item [{{item}}] by its role in the request.

criteria.context: Asks for no work of its own: background, a goal statement, framing ("i want to add X", "can you:", "we use bun", how things work now), or a lead-in whose instruction applies to each of the items listed after it ("update these docs:", "add X for these providers:").
criteria.task: Asks for work: a change, fix, design, investigation, or answer — including a detail or constraint of such work, or one entry of a list a lead-in applies to.
criteria.wrapup: A follow-up over the whole request that runs after every other item: run the test suite or checks, commit, changelog or docs for everything.

coupled.instructions: The state is a user's request to a coding agent, split into numbered items. Two items are coupled when one worker must do them together or in sequence: they change the same file, function, command, or component (items the request places in one file or component are coupled even when the changes differ); one needs the other's result, design, decision, or new API; one renames or reshapes something the other touches; or one only refines, constrains, or explains the other. Items are independent when separate workers could do them at the same time in one checkout without either waiting for or overwriting the other. Are items [{{a}}] and [{{b}}] coupled?
